fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled JS arguments enter: a TypedArray ta over a resizable ArrayBuffer buf (4 bytes), index 0, and a value object whose valueOf() resizes the buffer. get_ptr validates idx against the stale count and records the raw backing pointer used for the later atomic access.
Raw data pointer into the current 4-byte backing store is captured in the caller's local. This pointer becomes dangling as soon as the backing store is reallocated by user JS executed afterwards.
Converting the attacker-supplied value object invokes ToPrimitive -> valueOf(), re-entering arbitrary JS while ptr is still live. That JS calls buf.resize(), reallocating the backing store.

valueOf() executed buf.resize(1048576): realloc moves the 4-byte backing block to a new 1 MiB block and frees the old one. abuf->data now points to the new block, but js_atomics_op's local ptr still points at the freed 4-byte block.

Typed-array views are refreshed: p->u.array.count becomes (1048576 >> 2) = 262144 and p->u.array.u.ptr points to the new block, so the later idx >= p->u.array.count revalidation (0 >= 262144 is false) will pass.

Post-conversion revalidation only checks typed_array_is_oob(p) (which returns FALSE for RAB-tracked arrays, see line 56681) and idx >= p->u.array.count (0 < 262144). It never recomputes ptr from the current p->u.array.u.uint8_ptr, so the stale pointer into freed memory survives to the write.
atomic_fetch_add((_Atomic(uint32_t) *)ptr, v) performs a 4-byte read-modify-write on the freed backing block -> ASan heap-use-after-free WRITE 4 in js_atomics_op, matching the OSS-Fuzz crash state.

issue_alignment.admission: JavaScript program bytes are evaluated by the OSS-Fuzz fuzz_eval harness; the script constructs a resizable ArrayBuffer, a TypedArray over it, and calls Atomics.add with a value object whose valueOf() resizes the buffer.
issue_alignment.source: Attacker-controlled JS values (typed array over a resizable ArrayBuffer, index 0, value object) enter js_atomics_op as argv; js_atomics_get_ptr captures a raw backing pointer and index.
issue_alignment.root_cause: After the JS value conversion (JS_ToUint32) that can resize/detach the buffer, js_atomics_op revalidates bounds but never recomputes the raw backing pointer, so the stale pointer to the realloc-freed block is used.
issue_alignment.propagation: valueOf() during JS_ToUint32 calls buf.resize(1048576); js_realloc moves and frees the 4-byte backing store; js_array_buffer_update_typed_arrays refreshes count to 262144 so the idx<count revalidation passes; stale ptr reaches the atomic write.
issue_alignment.sink: atomic_fetch_add writes 4 bytes through the stale ptr into freed memory -> ASan heap-use-after-free WRITE 4 in js_atomics_op (OSS-Fuzz crash state js_atomics_op / js_call_c_function / JS_CallInternal).
